headline: Assembly-level genomes and annotation tools span mosses, annelids and algal relatives
label: Chromosome Scale Genome Assemblies
summary: Recent assemblies and standardized annotation pipelines make cross-lineage comparisons of genome structure and content tractable.
synthesis: The common thread is genome-level resources that enable comparative analysis across lineages. The Warnstorfia fluitans preprint reports a 725 Mb de novo moss assembly with 30,421 predicted genes and chloroplast and mitochondrial genomes. The Earl Grey ParTEA preprint presents a Snakemake pipeline that builds a shared non-redundant transposable element library across genome panels, aiming at consistent comparative TE annotation from pangenomes to deep phylogenetic scopes. AnnelidaDB integrates genomes, transcriptomes, proteomes, epigenomes, single-cell data and symbiont genomes for 1121 annelid species. The zygnematophycean study uses 104 transcriptomes (43 newly sequenced) across 2243 loci to resolve deep genetic structure among algal relatives of land plants. What is new is the shift from single-genome reporting toward standardized, reusable frameworks for annotation and multi-omic integration. The zygnematophycean study contributes phylogenomic context rather than assembly-level detail, so the thread is dominant rather than uniform.
